text:
Sync_Engine — Extracted Question
Problem Statement
A local-first app keeps a copy of the server's data on every client. Each client subscribes to one live query over a single table, orders, and the server must push an update to that client whenever the client's query result could have changed.
There are n subscribed queries, numbered 1 to n.
Query i has the form:
SELECT * FROM orders WHERE <expression_i>
Each WHERE clause is supplied as a boolean expression tree rather than SQL text.
A leaf is a condition:
column op value
where op is one of:
=, >, <, >=, <=
An internal node is AND, satisfied when every child is satisfied.
An internal node is OR, satisfied when at least one child is satisfied.
Nodes may be nested to any depth.
The table then receives q write operations, applied in the order given.
After each write, report every query whose result could have changed, and no others.
A query is affected when:
INSERT — the inserted row satisfies the query's expression.
DELETE — the deleted row satisfies the query's expression.
UPDATE — the old row or the new row satisfies the query's expression.
Read the input from standard input and write the answer to standard output.
Input Format
The first line contains two integers:
n q
Next come n expression trees, one per query, in order of query ID.
A tree begins with an integer T, its node count, followed by T lines describing nodes 1 to T.
Node 1 is the root.
Each node line is one of:
AND k c1 c2 ... ck
An AND node with k children.
OR k c1 c2 ... ck
An OR node with k children.
COND column op value
A leaf condition.
The first token of a line determines its shape.
AND and OR are followed by a child count and exactly that many node indices.
COND is followed by exactly three tokens.
Therefore, the input can be consumed token-by-token with no lookahead.
Child indices refer to nodes of the same tree, and children do not need to follow their parent.
The indices alone define the structure.
The nodes are guaranteed to form a valid tree r
